claims.statement: Every job owns one meeting directory under the output root the user picked: recordings create a folder named after the recording (`YYYY-MM-DD HHMMSS 녹음`), transcriptions get one from `prepare_job_directory`, and imported transcripts are copied into one — so refinement, reveal, and minutes naming behave identically no matter how the meeting came into existence.

`create_meeting_directory` names the folder after the input's sanitized stem (`meeting_stem` → `sanitize_name` keeps alphanumerics including Hangul plus `-`, `_`, space; other characters become `-`), deduplicates collisions with ` 2`, ` 3`, … up to 100 attempts before `OUTPUT_PATH_ERROR`, adopts the existing folder when the input already sits at `{stem}/{stem}.wav` inside it, and canonicalizes the result inside the output root.

`Artifacts` (`src-tauri/src/domain/artifact.rs`) is the aggregate root for one meeting's outputs; all path access goes through `Artifacts::path_for(kind)`, and `Srt`, `SpeakerText`, `Checkpoint`, `Minutes` are the only `ArtifactKind` values, with `path_for` returning `None` for kinds the meeting lacks (surfaced as `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND` by the use case).

`ArtifactKind` is exposed end to end: the Rust serde snake_case enum maps to the frontend's `"srt" | "speaker_text" | "checkpoint" | "minutes"` type, and the webview's open-srt/open-txt/open-checkpoint/open-minutes actions call the `open_artifact` IPC command with those kinds.

`minutes_path` is a pure domain function that derives the sibling minutes name by stripping a trailing `_화자별` from the transcript stem (keeping the stem when absent) and appending `_회의록.md`; `refine_transcript` applies it to the target's `txt`, so imported and transcribed meetings produce minutes names by the same rule.

The `JobRegistry` holds a `Mutex<HashMap<Uuid, Artifacts>>` that is in-memory only: `transcribe`/`import_transcript` register artifacts on success, `refine_transcript` claims a fresh job id but calls `register_minutes(target, …)` so minutes attach to the target transcription's entry, and closing the app drops every artifact handle — persistence is deferred to the roadmap's per-folder `galpi-meeting.json` manifest and must not be added without revisiting this design.

A recording immediately owns its meeting folder: `recording_folder_name()` formats `YYYY-MM-DD HHMMSS 녹음`, `NativeRecorder.start_sync` creates that folder and writes `<folder>/<folder>.wav.part`, `stop_sync` renames the partial to `<folder>/<folder>.wav` and returns the canonical path, and cancel/discard removes the partial and the folder if left empty — which is why transcribing that `.wav` later adopts the same folder and its artifacts share one base name.

Output names are external behavior and must not change: `<name>.wav`, `<name>.srt`, `<name>_화자별.txt`, `<name>.aligned.v2.json` (engine-tagged checkpoint), and the derived `<base>_회의록.md` from `minutes_path` — both engine pipelines and the host agree on them, and the roadmap's library design pins the same artifact filenames.

Both engines publish `<name>.aligned.v2.json` but tag it with an `engine` field so a preset switch never reads the other engine's word timings: WhisperX accepts a checkpoint tagged `whisperx` or untagged (pre-tag legacy files stay readable), while Qwen3 requires exactly the `qwen3` tag and treats anything else as absent.

A reusable checkpoint skips only ASR and alignment; diarization, hallucination filtering, and srt/txt publication always run afterward in both pipelines — the checkpoint caches word timings, never speaker labels or the published files.

`prepare_job_directory` seeds a new job folder by scanning the output root's other meeting folders for the same `<stem>.aligned.v2.json` (regular file, canonicalized inside the root), copying the most recently modified one in — so a re-run of the same audio name in a deduplicated `meeting 2` folder reuses the earlier alignment work; transcript import does not seed a checkpoint.

The host treats worker-reported artifact paths as untrusted: `validate_artifacts`/`canonical_artifact` in transcription and `canonical_minutes` in refinement canonicalize each reported path and require it to stay inside the job directory, failing with `WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR` otherwise; the Qwen3 path additionally maps an empty checkpoint string in the completion event to `None`.

The worker publishes artifacts atomically (sibling `.tmp` files replaced via `os.replace` for checkpoint/srt/txt, and the same temp-then-replace discipline for minutes), and opening an artifact repeats containment at the OS boundary: `Application::open_artifact` resolves `path_for(kind)` from the registry and `ArtifactPort::open_file` re-canonicalizes the path against the meeting's output directory (`ARTIFACT_PATH_ERROR` outside, `OPEN_ERROR` on opener failure); `reveal_output` opens the meeting folder itself.

`import_transcript` copies an existing transcript into a fresh per-meeting folder so refinement, reveal, and minutes naming behave exactly like a transcribed meeting: it accepts only `.txt`/`.md` (`INVALID_TRANSCRIPT`), caps size at 20 MB (`TRANSCRIPT_TOO_LARGE`, sized to catch mistaken selections such as audio files), skips the copy when the input already lives at `<folder>/<name>`, and returns `Artifacts` with only `txt` and `output_directory` set — `srt`, `checkpoint`, `minutes`, and `source_audio` are all `None`.

The import use case claims the job slot before the copy (the cancel receiver is deliberately unused — an import is a file copy with no child process) and registers the resulting artifacts, making an import mutually exclusive with transcription while remaining refinable, revealable, and openable immediately; the frontend mirrors the shape by hiding the srt and checkpoint rows and enabling the augment panel from the copy alone, and opening srt/checkpoint on an import returns `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

`source_audio` is the only artifact whose timestamp is the day the meeting happened: refinement derives the minutes' meeting date from the audio's mtime (`recorded_on` → `--meeting-date`) rather than the transcript's timestamp, which is when transcription ran; an imported transcript has no `source_audio`, so the worker falls back to the transcript file's own mtime and imported minutes lose meeting-date grounding — the accepted cost of the copy-based import design.
